body:
Found by T217's review (2026-08-25), named in test/federation/channel-record-trust.test.ts's
header rather than built there: cursesOf filters curse records by neither author nor lawful
negation, so a stranger holding plain write standing can append a negation of the operator's
curse record and the next poll re-blesses the retired lens — at a serving door. The curse's
whole §46.3 promise is durability against exactly this ("the curse is recorded, because a
standing sync would otherwise silently undo it").

Build: cursesOf honors only operator-authored curse records and reads their negations through
lawfulNegated (the same two-filter discipline readChannels just adopted in T217). Rails
two-sided and at both levels: a stranger's lift-attempt leaves the curse binding (the next
sync does NOT re-bless; the door still refuses the lens) while the operator's own lift still
works; delta level pins the stranger's negation landed-and-inert.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A stranger's negation of a curse record leaves the curse in force across the next sync —
    the lens stays retired at the door (two-sided: the operator's lift still revives it).
    Verify: new test test/federation/curse-authority.test.ts.
(b) The stranger's negation is present in the ground and inert (delta level). Verify: same file.

Merge tier: repair — the reader stops honoring a strike the constitution never authorized.
Self-merge on the ordinary bar.
title: A write-granted stranger can lift an operator's curse — cursesOf has no author filter
